item.text: The visible Latin font is now set through Writer and saved. I’m doing one file-level check as well because DOCX can keep separate Western, Asian, and complex-script font fields; I’ll normalize those remaining font fields to Times New Roman too.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED
import shutil, tempfile, os
p = Path('/home/user/Desktop/Dublin_Zoo_Intro.docx')
backup = p.with_suffix('.docx.bak-font-change')
# Keep a one-off backup only if it does not already exist.
if not backup.exists():
    shutil.copy2(p, backup)
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix='.docx', dir=str(p.parent)) as tmp:
    tmp_path = Path(tmp.name)
with ZipFile(p, 'r') as zin, ZipFile(tmp_path, 'w', ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
    for item in zin.infolist():
        data = zin.read(item.filename)
        if item.filename.startswith('word/') and item.filename.endswith('.xml'):
            text = data.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            text = text.replace('Georgia', 'Times New Roman')
            data = text.encode('utf-8')
        zout.writestr(item, data)
os.replace(tmp_path, p)
print('normalized')
PY
